metadata.title: Claude, Month Heads Up.
metadata.purpose: Answer whether Claude wrote custom logic for the month-heads-up skill, using the skill's own documented mechanism as the case. Lands the carry-out that a skill is a pre-written file Claude reads and follows, not code Claude improvises, and that determinism (same input, same output) is both the guarantee and the limit.
metadata.anchor_pair: B02 -> B03 (the 'month check · 25th · 30-day horizon' request, submitted, walked through the same three steps, run twice, then run again at a 60-day horizon)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes Claude built the month-heads-up skill itself, writing the cash-flow logic on the fly. It didn't. Claude reads a file someone else wrote and follows it, step by step. What's actually in that file?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'Claude built the month-heads-up skill. Right?', hesitates on 'built', corrects to 'reads', lands the real question

props.text:
Claude built the
month-heads-up
skill.
Right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('built' -> 'reads') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Open the month-heads-up folder and there's no hidden script computing the cash-flow numbers. One item sits there: SKILL.md — about two kilobytes of plain language. Claude reads that file itself and treats it as the program. There's nothing else in there to find.

shot.new_visual_element: A folder listing opens to exactly one item — SKILL.md — nothing else; the tile highlighted as the program itself

production_viz.label: No hidden script — one item, that's all
production_viz.mechanic: A folder icon opens onto exactly one tile: SKILL.md (2k). No second tile appears no matter how long the frame holds. The tile is outlined and a caption pins under it: 'this file IS the program.'

beats.narration_text: The pipeline lives in the Steps section, and Claude runs it top to bottom — linear, no branching unless a step says so. Ask it for the month check on the 25th with the default 30-day horizon, and it reads the SKILL.md, works through each step in order, and flags what needs attention before month-end.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR — a 'month check · 25th · 30-day horizon' request goes in, three ordered steps light up in sequence, an output card comes out

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR — request in, steps in order, output out
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A request card 'month check · 25th · 30-day horizon' enters from the left. Three numbered step tiles (STEP 1, STEP 2, STEP 3) light up left to right, one at a time, never out of order. An output card labelled '30-DAY OUTLOOK — FLAGGED' appears on the right. THIS EXACT REQUEST AND STEP SEQUENCE RETURN AT B03.

beats.narration_text: Ask for that same 30-day check again, and the answer comes back identical — not because Claude re-examined the cash flow with fresh judgment, but because the exact same steps ran a second time. Switch the horizon to 60 days instead, and the output changes — not because the logic changed, but because a different input ran through those same fixed steps. Identical output on identical input doesn't prove understanding. A different horizon producing different output doesn't prove the logic changed either.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — the same 30-day request submitted twice, two identical output cards; beside it, a 60-day horizon request producing a different card from the same three steps

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS — same input twice, then a different horizon
production_viz.mechanic: THE B02 REQUEST RETURNS, identical, run through the same three step tiles again. Two '30-DAY OUTLOOK — FLAGGED' output cards sit side by side, character-for-character identical. Beside them, a third run: 'month check · 25th · 60-day horizon' enters the same three steps and exits as a visibly different output card, '60-DAY OUTLOOK — FLAGGED'. A caption under all three: 'same steps, every time — the input is what changes.'

beats.narration_text: A Claude skill isn't code Claude writes on the fly. It's a file someone already wrote, that Claude reads and follows the same way, every single time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Open the month-heads-up skill folder. Before you run anything, read me the SKILL.md and tell me, in your own words, what steps it says to follow, in order. Liam, in for Bear.
